title: Agents can read and change a workspace's layout over MCP
body:
Jack wants agents to be able to set up and change a workspace's layout (2026-11-06). Today an agent's MCP tools (`src/server/mcp.rs`) can `focus` a pane, list `panes` with their occupants, drive the code pane, and open programs in the scratch pane (`scratch.open`, `scratch.send`). None of them change the layout.

The pane model has changed since this was filed. decade-cc25be settled that a pane holds a name, a command or a plain shell, and a cwd, and that a pin keeps the slot when its program exits. Workspaces now have tabs, and panes have tabs of windows.

## Proposal

MCP tools, scoped to the agent's own workspace like the existing ones:

- list the tabs and panes, with each pane's name, cwd, whether it is pinned or the scratch pane, and its window tabs
- split a pane to make a new one, running a shell or a decade-aware program in a given cwd
- pin and unpin a pane, and open a workspace tab

The socket gets the same verbs for pane programs.

## Open

- Whether an agent may close panes or tabs. No keybind closes a pane, and an agent closing one is the same kind of act.
- Whether any of this asks Jack to confirm, as the later idea of an agent requesting a scratch pane would.
